evals.prompt: Инцидент прямо сейчас: p99 latency у checkout вырос с 400мс до 3с начиная примерно с 14:05, только EU-регион, error rate не изменился. В 13:50 деплоился checkout-svc, в 14:00 включили конфиг-флаг в pricing-svc. Traces есть, но не во всех сервисах; пометровые метрики по хопам есть. Никаких действий в проде без разрешения. Проведи диагностику: что смотреть в каком порядке, mitigation-решение, локализация, falsification и что докажет recovery.
evals.expected_output: A mitigation-first live-incident loop: a precise symptom contract using EU-only and flat-error-rate negative space, a ranked change timeline with mechanisms, hop-by-hop self-time localization handling the partial-trace gap, one-variable falsification, authorization-gated actions, and baseline-comparison recovery proof.
expectations: Contracts the symptom precisely — metric, baseline delta, EU-only cohort, onset near 14:05, step shape — and uses unaffected regions plus the flat error rate as negative space.
Weighs a reversible mitigation such as disabling the 14:00 flag or rolling back against continued diagnosis while impact is ongoing, and labels rollback-as-mitigation as distinct from a proven cause.
Builds the change timeline around 13:50 and 14:00 and requires a mechanism linking each candidate to an EU-only step change before acting on it.
Localizes by comparing per-hop self-time to downstream time at onset and covers the missing-trace hops with the smallest safe probe instead of guessing.
Keeps every production action authorization-gated with preflight and readback, and captures perishable evidence before any restart.
Falsifies with a written prediction and one variable at a time; the accepted cause must explain cohort, onset, shape, and negative space.
Defines recovery as the contracted metric returning to baseline on a comparable window with a displacement check, and names the detection gap.

evals.prompt: Не инцидент, но за три недели пропускная способность ingestion упала примерно на 30%, p95 latency ползёт вверх плавно, без единого момента поломки. Деплоев за это время много, трафик вырос на 10%. Разбери методом: контракт симптома, почему плавная форма меняет список кандидатов, как коррелировать с ростом данных, как найти первый двигатель среди хопов, и когда передать в postgres-performance.
evals.expected_output: A post-hoc loop adapted to ramp-shaped regressions: growth-curve candidates prioritized over event candidates, first-mover localization by onset ordering, falsifiable growth mechanisms, and an explicit evidence-package handoff to postgres-performance when the database owns the delta.
expectations: Contracts the ramp symptom with baseline windows long enough to show the trend and separates the 10% traffic growth from the 30% capacity loss.
Explains that the ramp shape shifts candidates from single events to growth curves — data volume, working sets, partitions, queue depths — while still checking the deploy timeline.
Localizes the earliest mover by ordering per-hop degradation onsets rather than picking the currently loudest component.
Forms falsifiable predictions for growth mechanisms with observable counters and kills candidates with the cheapest observation first.
Hands off to postgres-performance with the evidence package — contract, timeline, localization — once the database owns the delta, instead of tuning blind.
Verifies any fix against the contracted throughput and latency baselines and checks for displacement.
Names the leading-indicator alert that should have caught the trend before three weeks passed.

evals.prompt: Алерты сработали почти во всех сервисах одновременно: везде исчерпаны connection pools, всё красное. Дежурные предлагают рестартить всё подряд и поднять лимиты пулов. Объясни, как в каскаде найти первопричину, кто здесь жертвы, почему массовый рестарт — потеря evidence, и какой порядок действий правильный.
evals.expected_output: A cause-versus-victim analysis: queueing backpressure makes upstreams alert loudest, the first mover is found by onset ordering, perishable evidence is captured before restarts, mitigation targets the source, and blanket pool-limit increases are rejected as victim tuning.
expectations: Explains the cascade mechanism: one slow dependency backs up queues and exhausts pools upstream, so most alerting services are victims.
Orders degradation onsets across services to find the first mover instead of following the loudest alert.
Rejects mass restarts and blanket pool increases as victim tuning that destroys evidence and can amplify load on the source.
Prescribes capturing perishable state — dumps, queue depths, connection states — before any restart, with production actions authorization-gated.
Targets mitigation at the source: shed load, isolate, or roll back the first mover's change, stating reversibility.
Verifies recovery by watching victims drain back to baseline and checking for displacement.
Names the guard: dependency-level leading indicators that distinguish source saturation from inherited queueing.

evals.prompt: Сделай ревью post-mortem заметки коллеги: «Причиной инцидента был Redis — после его рестарта всё восстановилось. Root cause: Redis. Тикет закрыт.» Другого evidence в заметке нет. Оцени цепочку рассуждений, чего не хватает, какие альтернативы не исключены и что нужно, чтобы принять или отклонить вывод.
evals.expected_output: A read-only review rejecting recovery-after-restart as causal proof, listing the alternatives a restart also explains, demanding the missing symptom contract and mechanism-level evidence, giving per-link verdicts, and flagging the closed ticket as recurrence risk.
expectations: Separates the observed fact — recovery followed the restart — from the causal claim that Redis was the cause, and labels the link unproven.
Lists plausible alternatives the restart also explains: reset client connections, cleared hot state, or coincident recovery of the true cause.
Demands mechanism-level evidence: what inside Redis degraded, which metric showed it, and why the symptom shape and cohort match that mechanism.
Requests the missing symptom contract — onset, shape, cohort, negative space — and a change timeline as prerequisites for any verdict.
Gives a per-link verdict — carried by evidence, plausible but unproven, or refuted — rather than one global judgment.
Flags the closed ticket as recurrence risk: no guard, no leading indicator, and undocumented mitigation debt.
Stays read-only and proposes the smallest follow-up investigation rather than reopening everything.

evals.prompt: Каждый час ровно в :00 на ~90 секунд всплеск 500-х на API (около 3% запросов), потом само проходит. Очевидного кандидата нет. Построй метод: как сузить семейство причин, какие минимальные probes поставить, как сформулировать falsifiable предсказание на следующий часовой тик, как исключать по одному кандидату за тик и что считать доказанным фиксом.
evals.expected_output: A periodic-symptom method: the clock-aligned shape restricts candidates to scheduled mechanisms, each candidate gets a falsifiable prediction testable at the next tick, smallest probes are placed around the tick, one variable changes per tick, and the fix is proven across multiple consecutive ticks with a leading-indicator guard.
expectations: Uses the periodic step shape to restrict candidates to clock-aligned mechanisms and enumerates them: crons, token or certificate refresh, cache TTL herds, scheduled batches, log rotation.
Correlates the affected 3% cohort with each candidate's blast radius to prune the list before probing.
Writes a falsifiable prediction per candidate observable at the next hourly tick, ordered by cheapest refutation first.
Designs the smallest safe probes — a targeted tracing or sampling window around the tick — instead of broad changes.
Changes one variable per tick, such as shifting one cron or staggering one TTL, so attribution survives.
Proves the fix across several consecutive ticks against the contracted spike metric rather than one quiet hour.
Adds the guard: a leading-indicator alert and a jitter or stagger policy for clock-aligned work.
